reference: No GNU scrub(1) CLI exists. Runnable operations are contract checks based on the scrub builtin's published help/source contract, POSIX ERE matching, and literal expected fixture contents/counts chosen independently of candidate output. Bash type/help metadata is checked against Bash's builtin metadata behavior.
coverage: Bash type -t and help metadata for the registered builtin.
Default denylist behavior for password/token/API-key forms and benign case-sensitive text.
Custom POSIX ERE addition/listing, match boundaries, and enabled/disabled behavior.
Invalid ERE rejection with nonzero status and a diagnostic.
scrub-current using a relative private fixture selected via HISTFILE; verifies retained lines, kept/dropped counts, executable mode preservation, and temporary-file cleanup.
Missing relative history file is a successful no-op.
Deferred requirements for /proc/self/mem argv rewriting and interactive readline/PROMPT_COMMAND pruning.
exclusions: No parity cases: there is no matching GNU scrub command, so scrub behavior is tested honestly as a contract rather than by substituting a different CLI.
scrub-argv is not invoked because it writes this process's /proc/self/mem; a future disposable VM or narrowly scoped proc-memory mock is required.
scrub live is not invoked because prompt-time pruning needs a controlled PTY/readline history fixture that the declarative runner does not provide.
The suite does not test every POSIX ERE feature, pattern-table exhaustion, write/rename fault injection, concurrent history updates.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash reports scrub as a shell builtin without invoking an operation.
Confirm Bash help exposes the documented scrub verbs and safety-specific operation descriptions.
cases.script:
docs=$(help scrub)
[[ $docs == *'bash history scrub helper (Stage 36.B-lite).'* ]] || exit 1
[[ $docs == *'scrub add-pattern REGEX'* ]] || exit 1
[[ $docs == *'scrub scrub-current [FILE] [-V VAR]'* ]] || exit 1
[[ $docs == *'/proc/self/cmdline argv memory range'* ]] || exit 1
printf 'help contract verified\n'

cases.purpose: Check documented built-in redaction patterns, status pattern count, and benign case-sensitive lines.
cases.script:
scrub status
for line in \
  'curl --password=fixture-value' \
  'TOKEN=fixture-value' \
  'API_TOKEN=fixture-value' \
  'token=ordinary-lowercase' \
  'echo harmless'; do
  rc=0
  scrub scrub-line "$line" || rc=$?
  printf '%s\n' "$rc"
done

cases.purpose: Verify a custom POSIX ERE is listed and matches only the anchored digit-suffixed form.
cases.script:
scrub clear-patterns
scrub add-pattern '^blocked[0-9]+$'
scrub list-patterns
for line in blocked42 blockedx xblocked42; do
  rc=0
  scrub scrub-line "$line" || rc=$?
  printf '%s\n' "$rc"
done

cases.purpose: Verify disable temporarily permits a default-matching line while preserving the denylist, and enable restores matching.
cases.script:
scrub status
scrub disable
rc=0
scrub scrub-line '--password=fixture-value' || rc=$?
printf '%s\n' "$rc"
scrub status
scrub enable
rc=0
scrub scrub-line '--password=fixture-value' || rc=$?
printf '%s\n' "$rc"
scrub status
cases.stdout:
enabled=1 patterns=14 live=no dropped=0
0
enabled=0 patterns=14 live=no dropped=0
1
enabled=1 patterns=14 live=no dropped=0

cases.purpose: Check malformed POSIX ERE input is rejected with failure and a diagnostic.
cases.script:
scrub clear-patterns
rc=0
scrub add-pattern '[' || rc=$?
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]] || exit 1
printf 'invalid ERE rejected\n'

cases.purpose: Redact a disposable relative HISTFILE, verify the documented kept/dropped count and retained content, and check rename cleanup and preservation of an executable mode bit. Independently inspect every permission bit with stat and emit all retained file bytes.
cases.script:
scrub clear-patterns
scrub add-pattern '^DROP='
umask 077
printf 'KEEP=one\nDROP=fake-fixture-secret\nKEEP=two\n' > history
chmod 751 history
HISTFILE=history
export HISTFILE
scrub scrub-current -V counts
[[ $counts == '2 1' ]] || exit 1
mapfile -t rows < "$HISTFILE"
[[ ${#rows[@]} -eq 2 ]] || exit 1
[[ ${rows[0]} == 'KEEP=one' && ${rows[1]} == 'KEEP=two' ]] || exit 1
[[ -x history ]] || exit 1
[[ ! -e history.scrub.tmp ]] || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$counts"
stat -c '%a' history
printf '%s\n' 'history bytes:'
while IFS= read -r row; do printf '%s\n' "$row"; done < history

cases.purpose: Check scrub-current treats a nonexistent relative history path as a no-op without creating it.
cases.script:
scrub clear-patterns
scrub scrub-current absent-history
[[ ! -e absent-history ]] || exit 1
[[ ! -e absent-history.scrub.tmp ]] || exit 1
printf 'missing history is a no-op\n'

cases.purpose: Future coverage should verify argv label truncation and zero-padding only within a disposable test shell process.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or narrowly scoped /proc fixture that supplies this test process's /proc/self/stat and writable /proc/self/mem, and independently inspects only the child fixture's argv bytes. The current runner's proc mount is read-only; this suite must not mutate host or runner process memory.

cases.purpose: Future coverage should verify pruning of curated in-memory history and PROMPT_COMMAND installation/restoration under a controlled prompt cycle.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM providing the following prerequisite: Requires a dedicated disposable PTY/readline harness with synthetic history and a bounded prompt cycle to verify pruning, dropped counts, and PROMPT_COMMAND save/restore. The declarative runner has no PTY interaction and must not touch a real login history.

cases.purpose: Empty history yields zero counts; disabled rewriting leaves literal bytes and returns documented pass marker.
cases.script:
scrub clear-patterns
: > empty
scrub scrub-current empty -V counts
printf '%s\n' "$counts"
printf 'KEEP\n' > history
scrub disable
scrub scrub-current history -V counts
printf '%s\n' "$counts"
IFS= read -r row < history
printf '%s\n' "$row"
